page: Microsoft Azure NCC40ads_H100_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance configured for intensive artificial intelligence, machine learning, and scientific computing workloads. Based on the x86_64 architecture using AMD processors, the server allocates 40 dedicated vCPUs alongside 320 GB of system memory, establishing a generous ratio of 8 GB RAM per core. The hardware platform is orchestrated through the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Hardware acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU equipped with 94 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. For fast scratchpad access and intermediate caching, the instance includes 1100 GB of local SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent disk requirements. The substantial 94 GB accelerator frame buffer provides high resource efficiency for single-GPU deployment strategies, reducing the operational overhead of distributing medium-scale models across multiple smaller cards.

Tradeoffs include the omission of complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which necessitates explicit virtual network routing or elastic IP allocation for ingress and egress connectivity. The instance is suited for deep learning training, large language model inference, AI fine-tuning, high-performance computing simulations, and high-throughput computer vision pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure NCC40ads_H100_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine belonging to the NCCads2023 series, engineered for high-demand machine learning and computational workloads. Powered by AMD x86_64 processors, the instance delivers 40 dedicated vCPUs paired with 320 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is anchored by a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU featuring 94 GB of VRAM, paired with 1100 GB of bundled local SSD storage and Premium Storage capability. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides dense compute and memory capacity for scenarios where standard virtual machines face accelerator bottlenecks. The substantial GPU memory eliminates common tiling and batch constraints during model serving. This configuration is tailored for deep learning training, large language model inference, molecular modeling, and data-intensive computer vision pipelines.
